clue.text: Crewman showing little variation in stroke

indicators.note: a small variation of the word stroke means its letters are reshuffled, here barely moved

explanation.surface: A rowing crewman whose stroke hardly changes from one pull to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little variation in' signals an anagram of STROKE; only the R moves. 'Crewman' sounds like a rower, but the crewman here shovels coal on a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker is a member of a ship's crew who feeds the boiler fires.

clue.text: Indecision shows us soft in reason

indicators.note: the pieces are placed within the word for reason, so in marks a container

parts.note: reason, as in good sense, gives sense
taken as written
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Being undecided shows that we are too soft to listen to reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reason' here is the noun sense of good judgement, not a cause or motive.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the uncertain state of waiting for an outcome, a kind of not knowing which way things will go.

clue.text: One who talks one round to see a musical drama

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A talkative person goes to watch a musical show.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale musical composition on a sacred story, sung like an opera but without staging.

clue.text: Terrible ache in a head

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase meaning per person

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters of ache are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as the fodder; that the letters also run across Terrible ache is a coincidence the parse does not use

explanation.surface: An awful pain inside one's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' looks like part of the headache picture, but means 'per person', as in 'five pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging so much each is charging per person, the same as so much a head.

clue.text: Time soon modifies feelings

indicators.note: to modify is to alter, so the letters of time and soon are rearranged

explanation.surface: With time, one's feelings change before long.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotions are states of feeling such as joy or grief.

clue.text: Girl goes on a journey, her first

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a ship, called she, making her first trip

parts.note: a maiden is a girl or young unmarried woman
a voyage is a journey, especially by sea

explanation.surface: A young woman sets off travelling for the first time in her life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' seems to be the girl, but ships are 'she', so 'her first' is a ship's first trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's inaugural crossing is called its maiden voyage.

clue.text: Payment for ring

definitions.meaning: a charge paid to use a road or bridge
to sound a bell slowly, as for a funeral

explanation.definitionFit: A toll is both a fee charged for passage and the slow, measured ringing of a bell.

clue.text: A prayer of three short words

parts.note: the answer splits into three little English words, the first meaning either, the second a form of be, the third meaning upon

explanation.surface: A brief prayer made up of just three little words.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into OR + IS + ON, three short words.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old literary word for a prayer, used by Shakespeare in Hamlet.

clue.text: Spectacles used by marksmen

explanation.definitionFit: Sights are both notable places to see and the aiming aids fitted on a gun.

clue.text: Occasion when spirits are called for

definitions.text: Occasion when spirits are called for

parts.words: Occasion when spirits are called for
parts.note: reads like a moment to order drinks at the bar, but the spirits are ghosts summoned by a medium

explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting where a medium tries to contact the dead.

clue.text: The author is not in

definitions.meaning: Henry ..., the English novelist who wrote Tom Jones
in cricket, the side that is not batting (not in) is out in the field

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'in'; the other team is fielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding was an eighteenth-century novelist, and fielding is what a cricket team does when its opponents bat.

clue.text: Aware of a rising sea, but far from queasy

definitions.meaning: sensing the heave of a sea wave beneath you
in very good health, the opposite of seasick

explanation.definitionFit: To feel a swell is to sense a big wave rolling, and to feel swell is slang for being in fine health.

clue.text: Mark comes back to school

indicators.note: coming back means the word for mark is read in the other direction

parts.note: to note something is to mark it

explanation.surface: A grade is returned to a pupil at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns NOTE into the answer. Eton is a famous English private school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known English boarding school.

clue.text: Nerve broken? Not at all!

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of nerve are put back together differently

explanation.surface: Has your courage cracked? Absolutely not!
explanation.definitionFit: Never is an emphatic way of saying 'not in any way'.

clue.text: Left or right in the vessel

definitions.text: Left or right in the vessel

parts.words: Left or right in the vessel
parts.note: names the left-hand side of a ship, or a fortified wine poured into a decanter

explanation.definitionFit: Port is the left side of a ship when facing forward, and also a fortified Portuguese wine served from a decanter.

clue.text: As good and bad employees may be, with enthusiasm

definitions.text: As good and bad employees may be
definitions.meaning: keen workers are inspired, poor workers are sacked
as in filled with enthusiasm, ablaze with keenness

explanation.definitionFit: A dismissed worker has been sacked, and an eager worker is inspired with zeal: the same word covers both.

clue.text: Quick to catch five in a falsehood

indicators.note: the five is set within the lie, so in marks the container

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Being caught out in a lie about the number five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' means living, as in 'the quick and the dead', not fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The quick is an old term for the living, as opposed to the dead.

clue.text: Flat-finding agencies

parts.note: sounds like firms that find apartments to rent, but means tools that show whether a surface is horizontal

explanation.definitionFit: A builder's bubble tool shows whether a surface is truly horizontal.

clue.text: Getting down to making a proposal?

definitions.text: Getting down to making a proposal?

parts.words: Getting down to making a proposal?
parts.note: getting down to means starting on, but here it is literally lowering oneself on to one knee to ask for marriage

explanation.definitionFit: A traditional suitor goes down on one knee to ask for someone's hand.

clue.text: The smartest form of bedding

indicators.note: a new form of the word smartest means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The most fashionable kind of bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded base of a bed, part of its bedding.

clue.text: Navy planes in sorry state

indicators.note: a sorry state is a bad condition, so the letters of navy planes in are in disarray

explanation.surface: The navy's aircraft are in a poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry state' reads as one phrase, but 'sorry' is the anagram signal and 'state' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennsylvania is one of the US states.

clue.text: No part exchange for this customer

indicators.note: exchanging places swaps the letters of no part around

explanation.surface: This shopper is not allowed any part-exchange deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part exchange' looks like a trade-in; 'part' is fodder and 'exchange' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular customer of a shop or restaurant.

clue.text: To extract information is illegal, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the word for illegal is said aloud

parts.note: illicit means illegal

explanation.surface: Prying information out of someone is against the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit information is to draw it out of someone.

clue.text: Backward island not lacking in skill

indicators.note: backward means the name of the island is read from right to left

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: An island that is behind the times but not short of talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' suggests slow, but it reverses ELBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means competent, having the necessary skill.

clue.text: Practice gives us time

parts.note: taken as written
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Training gives us extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the way something is habitually done.

clue.text: Experienced hat-maker

definitions.meaning: the pressed woollen cloth from which hats are made

explanation.definitionFit: Felt is both the past tense of 'feel' and the matted fabric used for trilbies and fedoras.

clue.text: Exude an air of sadness

parts.note: reads as seeming gloomy, but literally means breathing out a sad breath

explanation.definitionFit: A sigh is a long, audible breath out expressing sorrow or weariness.

clue.text: Push money over bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: p, for penny or pence, is a unit of British money
a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: Shoving cash across a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to push or poke someone.

clue.text: A criminal picked up in response to a telephone call

definitions.text: picked up in response to a telephone call
definitions.meaning: the handset lifted when the phone rings

explanation.definitionFit: A fence who takes stolen goods is a receiver, and so is the earpiece of a telephone.

clue.text: Reach a swirling river

indicators.note: swirling water churns about, so the letters of river are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting to a river full of whirlpools.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive somewhere is to reach it.

clue.text: Bananas he will put in fruit container

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, as is nuts
he'll is the contraction of he will

explanation.surface: He will put bananas in the fruit bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' and 'fruit' suggest a fruit bowl, but 'Bananas' means mad, NUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut's hard outer case holds its kernel, the edible fruit.

clue.text: Sayings of modern times

parts.note: AD (anno domini) marks the modern era, after BC
ages are long periods of time

explanation.surface: Proverbs from the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are proverbs, traditional sayings.
